items.label: Margin of Safety vs measured share

blocks.text: The connections clearing fastest are non-firm — interruptible by contract. The market prices damage; the peril is availability.

Britain is reconnecting industry to a network that cannot promise firm power at queue speed. Data centres and grid-scale assets contract for always-on availability while the connections that clear retain the operator's right to curtail under Gate 1 terms.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}} That gap — between what the asset loses and what the policy pays — is the subject of this index.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Reindustrialisation and compute build-out are not waiting for firm connections. Demand-side reform is consulting on the right to curtail very large users; the queue already runs to triple-digit gigawatts.{{cite:OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} The peril is no longer a tail event in a hazard module — it is a register fact on the connection agreement.

We scored {{fact:total}} UK insurance-market participants — {{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs and brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} reinsurers — on Exposure to non-firm load and Preparedness to underwrite it, then reduced each to a single number: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure.

How large is the bet? Exposure asks how much of the book, portfolio, or asset base sits on interruptible connections — and how correlated that concentration is when a constraint event bites more than one insured at once.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA,PRA-PPP}}

Five sub-factors carry the score: book concentration on energy and compute, non-firm intensity (from TEC gate status and embedded-capacity registers where measured), aggregation on shared grid geography, the trigger gap between damage-BI wordings and curtailment loss, and tenor mismatch between multi-year cover and a peril with almost no claims history.

blocks.text: Can this entity actually carry the risk it has written? Preparedness is not capital alone — it is whether the form, the data, and the pricing model see curtailment as a first-class peril rather than a property-damage footnote.{{cite:LLOYDS-PARAMETRIC-CYBER,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

Product fit is the hinge: parametric availability triggers, SLA mirrors, and curtailment indices exist in fragments; most carrier wordings still wait for physical damage. Underwriting expertise, telemetry, reinsurance depth, and pricing models must span power and interruption — not cat hazard footprints.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}}

blocks.kicker: MARGIN OF SAFETY VS MEASURED SHARE

blocks.text: A large positive margin on assessed inputs alone is a hypothesis, not a finding. The scatter below plots Margin of Safety against each entity's measured/disclosed share — the epistemic hygiene the L5 publication gate enforces. At {{fact:measured_pct}} blended measured share the index remains PROVISIONAL; regression slope will move as register tiers land.

blocks.caption: Each dot is one entity. Measured share = blend-weighted deterministic input.

blocks.text: The stack carries different parts of the same correlated cluster. Carriers (L1) average a modest positive margin; underlying assets (L3) show the deepest negative spreads — exposure on Gate-1 connections runs ahead of any single carrier's preparedness score.{{fact:l1}} carriers · {{fact:l2}} market participants · {{fact:l3}} assets · {{fact:l4}} reinsurers.

Heaviest exposed concentration sits in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}}. Whitespace carriers named in the current slice include {{fact:whitespace_l1_names}} — the placement question is not whether capacity exists, but whether wordings match the peril.

blocks.text: Segment tags (energy, data centre, parametric MGA, broker, reinsurance) expose where the margin compresses — data-centre and energy assets carry the most negative means; parametric and broker layers sit closer to neutral because product design already chases non-damage triggers.

blocks.text: At carrier level, exposure and preparedness diverge in ways the headline score hides. A syndicate with strong capital and weak register measurement can sit in whitespace on assessed inputs alone — until Gate 2 status lands on a linked asset and the deterministic tier moves.

Cat models are the wrong architecture: there is no licensable hazard module for lawful switch-off. The correlated loss is geographic and contractual — shared constraint boundaries and damage-only triggers — not a seismic zone or wind footprint.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Select a carrier: each dot is one underlying asset positioned by its Margin of Safety; the dashed line is the carrier average. A diversified renewable or DC book can look adequate at the syndicate level while linked assets cluster exposed — aggregation the headline MoS does not show.

blocks.text: The market's conventional answer — property damage plus business interruption — fires on breakage. Curtailment loss is contractual: the operator exercises a lawful right to interrupt, the asset breaches an SLA, and revenue stops with the plant intact.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}}
Basis risk is not a modelling refinement — it is the gap between the peril and the trigger. Until availability is indexed to register-native measurement, every curtailment hour is an unfunded loss.

blocks.caption: Two paths: damage-BI (left) pays; curtailment (right) often does not.

blocks.text: The index is not the product. It is the wedge: register-native measurement of a peril the market underwrites blind — so the cover that closes the trigger gap can be priced, reinsured, and placed with eyes open.{{cite:NESO-TEC,FCA-PRIN}}

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

Brokers and MGAs have already placed parametric and SLA structures around DC and renewable risk — the line forming around the gap, not yet a full carrier stack.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

blocks.caption: Market responses already in force — click through to source.

blocks.text: Gate 1 and Gate 2 made firmness a register fact — not a negotiating point.{{cite:NESO-CMP434}} CMP448 priced progression into the Gate-2 queue from January 2026.{{cite:NESO-CMP448}} Demand-side reform is consulting on curtailment rights for the largest users. The rules landed before the market repriced who can carry the interruptible half.

Brokers have placed billion-dollar DC facilities on non-firm terms; the constraint cost curve is observable in NESO data while BI rates on damage triggers stay flat. That combination — rising physical cost, flat premium on the wrong peril — is the definition of mispricing.
